newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland mine leases face delay - premier.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland mine leases face delay - premier.

text.p: Queensland premier Rob Borbidge said on Friday mining companies seeking land title security on their leases in the state faced lengthy delays because of right-to-negotiate provisions of Australia's Native Title Act.

"Now that there is a general understanding, short of legislative action by the Commonwealth (Federal government), that any pastoral lease might be subject to native title, all new and re-issued mining leases must engage the right-to-negotiate process," Borbidge said in a statement.
"This is untenable for industry and all governments until it is remedied."
Borbidge said mining companies could face delays of up to 14 months under the negotiation process with the possibility of further court challenges.
"Only projects significant enough to attract an eventual declaration from the Commonwealth that they should proceed in the national interest would have a ghost of a chance of proceeding," he said.

Borbidge and other conservative state premiers have been campaigning for changes to the Native Title Act following the High Court decision in December that pastoral leases might be subject to native title.
Some 40 percent of Australia's land area is covered by pastoral leases and many mining properties are on existing or former pastoral leases.

When the former Labor government passed the Native Title Act in late 1993, the preamble to the Act said it was assumed that pastoral leases overrode native title and until the High Court ruling, it was generally accepted that this was the case.
